name: N'Ko (Manding koiné)
notes: N'Ko (ߒߞߏ), the Manding literary koiné written in the N'Ko script devised by Solomana Kanté in 1949. INPUT CONTRACT: native N'Ko-script text (Unicode block U+07C0..U+07FF, NFC), written RIGHT-TO-LEFT; no romanisation is accepted. N'Ko is an ALPHABET (not an abjad or abugida): seven vowel letters (ߊ ߋ ߌ ߍ ߎ ߏ ߐ) and nineteen consonant letters are written in full, plus combining diacritics. Tone and vowel length are written with seven combining marks (U+07EB..U+07F1): they are mapped to IPA tone letters (and ː for the long series) rather than to segments; an unmarked vowel is short with a falling tone. U+07F2 (nasalisation) maps to a combining tilde. ߑ DAGBASINNA is a silent letter marking the absence of a vowel in a consonant cluster and maps to the empty string. LEFT OUT ON PURPOSE: U+07F3 (double dot above) and the JONA letters ߨ ߩ ߪ, which modify a base letter for non-native sounds in loans — their value depends on the base letter and no single segmental value can be assigned.
